content:
Zoe Park: hey folks, day 1 done but i can't pull our base image from the internal registry after VPN connect: `docker pull registry.internal.redwood:5000/base:latest` fails with TLS error. getting `x509: certificate signed by unknown authority`. anyone seen this during onboarding?

Claire Sun: welcome Zoe! are you on a company laptop or personal? company images usually trust our internal CA which is installed by Intune on managed devices. If personal, you need to add the corporate root CA to your system and Docker.

Zoe Park: personal macbook. i did the Okta SSO -> Tunnel and it shows connected. `curl -v https://registry.internal.redwood:5000/v2/` shows certificate chain but my mac says unknown issuer.

Ravi Singh: that lines up. The VPN pushes routes but not machine-level certs for personal devices (we don't auto-install roots). Quick checks: 1) confirm `openssl s_client -showcerts -connect registry.internal.redwood:5000` to see the CA chain; 2) if it's our internal CA, download the root cert from our intranet and add to Keychain (System, Always Trust).

Zoe Park: ran openssl and the issuer CN is "Redwood Internal CA". i googled and found the pem on the onboarding portal but when i import to Keychain and mark Always Trust, docker still errors.

Claire Sun: Docker Desktop on mac uses its own trust store for the daemon (especially if using the Hyperkit VM). Try adding the CA to Docker's certs: `mkdir -p ~/Library/Containers/com.docker.docker/Data/vms/0 && cp redwood-ca.crt ~/Library/Containers/com.docker.docker/Data/certs/` or for newer Docker Desktop: Preferences -> Resources -> Proxies -> Add certs, then restart Docker. Alternatively add the CA to /etc/ssl/certs and restart the docker daemon.

Zoe Park: tried copying to `~/Library/.../Data/certs/` and restarted Docker Desktop. `docker pull` now gives a different error: `unauthorized: authentication required`.

Ravi Singh: ok progress. That means TLS is fine now but you need to authenticate with our registry via Okta OIDC token. We have a small helper script that exchanges Okta session for a docker token: `docker-login-internal.sh` in the onboarding repo. Try `./docker-login-internal.sh` and then `docker pull`.

Zoe Park: ran the script, it opened a browser for Okta auth and then `docker login registry.internal.redwood:5000` succeeded. pull works now. thanks!

IT Support: quick follow-up: because this was a personal device, security requires you to complete the device attestation checklist before we allow persistent registry push rights. You can still pull but we restrict write/push until IT verifies.

infra-bot: Created INFRA-5052: "Add note to onboarding: personal devices need manual root CA install + docker cert steps".

okta-bot: User Zoe Park (zoe.park@redwood.com) authenticated via Okta at 2026-01-04T09:12:07Z

security-bot: Reminder: do not add internal CA to devices you do not control long-term. For contractors or short-term personal devices, request a temporary dev image or use github codespaces.

Claire Sun: we'll add a one-click CA installer to the onboarding repo and document Docker Desktop steps. Also adding a FAQ entry: "Why do I see x509 unknown authority after VPN?"

Zoe Park: all set now, can clone repos that reference base image. appreciate the speedy help :raised_hands:
